volume.title: Merge
volume.author: spec-author seat, group G2, round 3; book 1.1.0 amendment

contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, schema, shared volumes
Input records: gate.verdict green plus review.passed on one head
Mechanism: merge.sh lifted into the Go service, with the fix-ticket exception under a hold
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries: three attempts, then recover and report
Many agents at once: the collision answer
State paths written and the cleanup script for each

related.note: the fix path whose pull request this node merges under a hold
the ticket entity whose hold_id field names the hold a fix ticket was cut for

pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book
forge-merge is this node's credential and no other node's
The protection N-09 requires before any merge call
The merge and update-branch calls are effects rows written in the deciding Commit
pr_open to merged here; merged to done only on a verified main (N-03, N-10)

purpose.sentence: When the newest head of a pull request carries a green coq/gate verdict and a review.passed record, main has no unverified merge, protection is verified and no hold stands, the Go service squash-merges it on GitHub with the forge-merge credential and writes one merge record with the merge sha and its parent on main, or brings the branch up to date, or writes one merge.conflict 409, and no seat is involved.
purpose.is: A pure function of records, the forge:snapshot entity and the clock (V03): the same inputs give the same decision, so two runs cannot disagree.

The machine verdict merge of D15: green gate plus reviewer record; the owner holds the line through cards and the Controls screen, never through the per pull request path, except for the owner-locked page assets (../N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm).

One unverified merge at a time (F13): a merge waits until every earlier merge on main has a verified or rejected record, so a main run is never superseded by the line's own merges and a red range is exactly one merge.
purpose.is-not: Not a merger seat: 43 of 92 merges were hand merges by an LLM seat that took about fifteen minutes each (L13 section 7 D11; merge.sh breadcrumb); the seat is retired (D11, C39).
Not a merge train: the roadmap ruling o71ee (never wait on a verify between merges) is superseded by the owner's pick for F13 and rejected below.
purpose.is: Under a merge.hold (N-10) exactly one kind of merge is allowed: the fix pull request whose ticket entity names the standing hold id (the hold exception, ../N-10/spec.xml#m-fix). Under the owner hold (flag:hold) exactly one kind is allowed: a pull request whose ticket belongs to the current bootstrap step (the bootstrap merge path, shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap-merge); the owner's break-glass merge through N-42 is the alternative.
purpose.decisions: D05 (C43), D11 (C39), D15 (C50), V03, T08, F13 owner pick (at most one unverified merge).

record.field: The pull request, its current head, its ticket and the status observation that made it green.
Must equal the verdict's; a review on an older head is held, never merged (merge.sh choice 1; gate.sh heads_match).

The reviewer run and its lease (shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_ref, key and integer token, as N-19 writes it); N-01 refused the record with 412 if the token was not current, so this node trusts the record.

input.reads: The forge:snapshot entity (mergeable, mergeable_state, base_sha, draft, head_sha, detail_at, deferred; ../N-04/spec.xml#output); forge_pr_files for (pr, head_sha); forge.pr_closed records; the newest protection.observed and protection.drift (N-04); merge records with no verified or rejected record (N-10); the newest merge.hold (N-10); flag:hold and the entity bootstrap:state (shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap); the ticket entity (N-03: hold_id, bootstrap step); the halt record; the merge.lock lease (N-02); the effects rows of this node (shared/contracts.xml#outbox).
input.starts-when: Both records exist for the same (pr, head_sha): the second to commit starts the traversal; every scheduler tick (N-07) re-examines every pull request with both records and no merge record, and every effects row of this node in sent or unknown, so a lost start or a lost reply is caught (level-triggered).

record.field: N-09/merge/<pr>@<head_sha>/r1 (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys); one merge record per head, ever.
Copied; base_sha is the PR's base.sha from the snapshot at the decision.
The squash commit on main and its first parent (the main sha it landed on), read back from GitHub.
Next value of N-01's counter in the same transaction; with linear history it orders merges on main (N-10).
The head branch, for N-45's branch deletion and worktree release.
forge_pr_files of (pr, head_sha), never truncated (step 3); N-47 and N-48 read them when N-10 verifies the merge.
At most one: the hold id when the merge landed by the hold exception; the bootstrap state when it landed by the bootstrap merge path.
GitHub accepted update-branch (it answers 202) for expected_head_sha head_sha; the new head it pushes needs its own gate verdict and review (step 5).
N-09/merge.conflict/<pr>@<head_sha>/r1; once per head (merge.sh choice 4); a new head re-arms it.
The conflict named, from mergeable_state dirty or from an update-branch refusal; carries the failure body of shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/failure_body.

github-unreachable, refused-by-branch-rule, unknown-outcome, read-back-failed or closed-unmerged; a system-lane fault, never a worker attempt (merge is not a ticket phase, shared/contracts.xml#roles).

merge-hold, owner-hold, stale-review, draft, not-mergeable-unknown, awaiting-owner-confirm (../N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm), awaiting-verify, protection-unverified, protection-mismatch, files-unknown, update-branch-limit, dark (merge.enabled false); written once per (pr, head, reason) so the Machine screen shows why a green pull request waits; it is not a failure.
Written once per hold id when a hold has stood longer than merge.hold_age_alert_seconds (wait w-hold); N-28 coalesces it with N-10's card by hold id.

output.ends-when: A merge, branch.update, merge.conflict or merge.failed record names the head; a merge.held ends this traversal and the next matching tick starts a new one.

mechanism.where: Go package merge inside the service, a port of line/bin/merge.sh with the same choices; every GitHub write goes through the outbox (shared/contracts.xml#outbox) with the forge-merge credential (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix: contents and pull requests write), which no other node holds; reads come from N-04's entity, so this node issues no poll of its own.
mechanism.step: Load the pull request's current head from the forge:snapshot entity (fresh: not stale, detail_at within forge.stale_after_seconds, nothing deferred for it; otherwise end, the next tick retries); load the newest gate.verdict and the newest review.passed for the ticket. Both must name that head and the verdict must be green; otherwise merge.held stale-review and end (gate.sh heads_match lifted).

Holds, read before any GitHub call and again inside the step 7 Commit, because N-10 and N-29 can write them during a slow traversal (merge.sh hold choice 2). flag:hold (the owner hold set by USERHALT through N-44, the hold lamp): merge.held owner-hold, except in bootstrap mode (shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap-merge, path default): from the proof of cut-over step 3 until B8, a pull request whose ticket has build-mode scope rebuild and belongs to a step the current entity bootstrap:state allows merges; its merge record carries bootstrap_step and every later step still applies (green gate and review on the same head, awaiting-verify, protection). Before step 3's proof no machine verdict exists, so those pull requests are the owner's break glass, one card each (path pre-gate); this node merges nothing for them. merge.hold (N-10, a red main): merge.held merge-hold, except the pull request whose ticket entity carries hold_id equal to the standing hold's hold_id (the fix N-10 step 5 cut, ../N-10/spec.xml#m-fix); that merge record carries fix_for_hold_id. A hold_id naming a lifted or unknown hold is a normal ticket.

At most one unverified merge on main (F13): if any merge record has neither a verified nor a rejected record (N-10), merge.held awaiting-verify with unverified_merge_seq, and end; no exception passes this step, the fix pull request included, because a fix on an unverified main would be judged in the same range. The wait is bounded by N-10's verify bound (shared/retry-budget.xml#deadlines d-verify): past it N-10 writes main.verify.missing and N-28 posts one card; this node keeps holding (fail closed).

Protection: the newest protection.observed (N-04) must be younger than two protection.check_seconds and no protection.drift may be newer (shared/authority.xml#github-app); otherwise merge.held protection-unverified and end. N-10 relies on the same record for linear history.

Files: forge_pr_files must hold the rows of (pr, head_sha) with files_truncated false; otherwise merge.held files-unknown and end (N-04 reads them on the next poll; a truncated list, over 3000 files, stays held and N-28 posts one card, because the owner-confirm rule cannot be decided on a partial list). Owner confirm: a pull request whose paths touch promotion.confirm_paths with no promotion.confirm ruling naming its current head is merge.held awaiting-owner-confirm (the one rule: ../N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm).

Take the merge.lock lease from N-02 (class work, merge.lock_seconds 300 from shared/contracts.xml#timing, one per repository, fencing token): it covers one call, its read-back and the acquire. Not granted: end; the next tick retries. Under the owner hold N-02 grants merge.lock only for the bootstrap merge path (shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine; shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap-merge).

Decide by mergeable_state from the entity, the one vocabulary of ../N-04/spec.xml#output. clean, unstable or has_hooks: step 8. dirty: merge.conflict 409 source mergeable-state-dirty to N-11 (a worker attempt with merge-main, shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner) and end. behind: step 7b. blocked with a green gate and a passed review: merge.held protection-mismatch, a poll_now to N-04 so protection is read again, and end (protection asks for something the line does not provide). draft: merge.held draft. unknown or mergeable null: merge.held not-mergeable-unknown; GitHub computes it on its own time and N-04 reads it again next poll.

behind (strict protection, main moved): PUT pulls/N/update-branch with expected_head_sha equal to head_sha, as an effects row with key N-09/branch.update/<pr>@<head_sha>/r1 written in the Commit that decides it. 202: branch.update 100; GitHub pushes a new head, which needs its own gate verdict and review.passed like any pushed head, so the line re-gates it. 422 expected head mismatch: end (the snapshot moves). 422 merge conflict: merge.conflict source update-branch-conflict. At most merge.update_branch_per_hour 3 per pull request; past it merge.held update-branch-limit until the hour rolls (a busy main is visible, not looped).

One merge call per head: the effects row N-09/merge/<pr>@<head_sha>/r1 (provider github, action pull.merge) is written in the Commit that re-reads the holds of step 2; then PUT pulls/N/merge with merge_method squash and sha equal to head_sha (GitHub refuses a head that moved, 409). 200: step 9. A refusal (405 not mergeable, 409 head moved, 422) is final for this head: the row is failed, the call is never sent again on the unchanged head; 405 writes merge.failed refused-by-branch-rule and a poll_now so N-04 reads protection and mergeable_state again, and the next decision is made on fresh state (behind goes to step 7b, blocked to protection-mismatch). A transport failure or timeout leaves the row unknown: step 8b.

Reconcile before any repeat (shared/contracts.xml#outbox): read GET pulls/N with forge-merge, or the forge.pr_closed record N-04 wrote when the PR left the open list. merged with merge_commit_sha: the merge landed; step 9 with already_merged true. Open, unmerged, same head: the call never took effect; it is sent again on the same row (attempts at most 3, shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/effect_row). Closed unmerged: merge.failed closed-unmerged. Unreadable after three reads: merge.failed unknown-outcome and the next tick reconciles again; the row stays unknown, so nothing is sent blind.

Read back the merge commit and its first parent; in one Commit write the merge record (merge_sha, parent_main, base_sha, merge_seq from N-01's counter, branch, paths from forge_pr_files), tickets.transition pr_open to merged (shared/contracts.xml#ticket-transitions; done comes only with N-10's verified), the effects row done with the merge sha as external id, and release merge.lock; then poll_now. The merge record is the input of N-26 and N-45; N-47, N-48 and N-35 act on N-10's verified for it, never on the merge (F13).

No branch deletion, no worktree, no slot return, no checkout of main here: those are N-45's cleanup.run with its own three attempts, because a cleanup that fails must never withhold a merge record (merge.sh post_merge_clean; SPEC-17 s-orchestrator O3 and H12).
mechanism.invariant: One merge record per head, one merge call per unchanged head, one merge.conflict per head, written by the service only; no seat holds forge-merge and N-01 refuses kind merge from any principal but the service.
GitHub is the second guard: a merge without green coq/gate from the coq-gate app is refused by the forge whatever this node does (D05, shared/authority.xml#github-app).
mechanism.diagram: flowchart TD I["gate.verdict green + review.passed on head H"] --> M{"both name the current head?"} M -- no --> HS["merge.held stale-review"] M -- yes --> HO{"halt, owner hold or merge.hold?"} HO -- "yes, no exception" --> HH["merge.held owner-hold or merge-hold"] HO -- "no, or bootstrap step, or the fix PR" --> UV{"a merge on main unverified?"} UV -- yes --> HV["merge.held awaiting-verify"] UV -- no --> PR{"protection.observed fresh, no drift?"} PR -- no --> HP["merge.held protection-unverified"] PR -- yes --> FL{"files known, owner confirm satisfied?"} FL -- no --> HF["merge.held files-unknown or awaiting-owner-confirm"] FL -- yes --> L{"merge.lock granted?"} L -- no --> E["end, next tick"] L -- yes --> MS{"mergeable_state"} MS -- dirty --> C["merge.conflict 409 to N-11"] MS -- behind --> UB["update-branch, branch.update 100; new head re-gated"] MS -- blocked --> HB["merge.held protection-mismatch"] MS -- "unknown or draft" --> HU["merge.held"] MS -- "clean, unstable, has_hooks" --> G["one merge call, sha = H (outbox)"] G -- merged --> R["merge 200, ticket merged"] G -- "no answer" --> RC["reconcile: GET pulls/N or forge.pr_closed"] RC -- merged --> R G -- refused --> F["merge.failed, never resent on H"] R --> N26["N-26 verify main; N-10 verified then N-47, N-48, N-35"]

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: The commit of the second of the two input records (N-01 record.committed) starts a traversal in the service; the scheduler tick (N-07) re-examines every pull request with both records and no merge record, and every effects row of this node not done, every tick, so a traversal lost to a crash restarts within one tick.
start.restart: After a crash step 8b finds a merge that landed before the record was written (an effects row in sent or unknown) and writes the record once.
start.never: No make merge target in the line path (T15 is an owner entry point only), no merger seat, no hand gh pr merge.

wait.fallback: end the traversal; the next tick retries; a lease held longer than merge.lock_seconds 300 expires by itself (N-02) so a crashed holder never blocks merges

wait.timeout: 20 s (gate.sh and route.sh used timeout 20 for gh; L01 section 6)
wait.fallback: the effects row goes unknown and step 8b reconciles before any repeat; never a blind retry

wait.on: reading the PR or the merge commit after a merge or an unknown outcome
wait.fallback: three reads with 2, 4, 6 s backoff inside merge.lock_seconds; then merge.failed read-back-failed or unknown-outcome; the next tick reconciles again; the merge stands

wait.timeout: none held: re-read every poll by N-04
wait.fallback: merge.held not-mergeable-unknown once per head, re-written once with count 3 after three polls so N-41 shows it; GitHub computes mergeability on its own time, so the fallback is visibility, not a guess

wait.on: the previous merge on main reaching verified or rejected (N-10)
wait.fallback: N-10 writes main.verify.missing and N-28 posts one card; this node keeps merge.held awaiting-verify (fail closed) until N-10 writes a verdict or the owner's break glass through N-42
merge.held protection-unverified; N-04's protection.drift card asks the owner to repair protection with forge-admin

wait.on: merge.hold lifted by N-10 (a green main after the fix merge)
wait.fallback: the wait is never on a person: the fix pull request merges under the hold by the step 2 exception; at the bound merge.hold.aged 500 is written once per hold id to N-41 and N-28 (coalesced with N-10's card by hold id) and non-fix merges stay held, because a red main must fail closed

waits.rule: Every GitHub call carries a context deadline and its operation key; a repeat after an unknown outcome goes through step 8b, never a blind retry (doc 31: reconcile by stable idempotency key before replaying a mutation, L14 section 4.6).

step.name: GitHub merge call
step.attempts: 1 per unchanged head; a transport failure is re-sent on the same effects row only after step 8b proves it never took effect (at most 3 sends)
step.then: merge.failed 500 to N-41 and one card by N-28; a refusal is never repeated on the same head

step.name: read back
step.then: merge.failed read-back-failed; the next traversal completes the record (step 8b)

step.name: record write
step.then: store.unreachable 500 once; the next traversal rewrites it from the read back with the same operation key

retries.not-retried: A merge.conflict is not retried by this node: the fix is a worker attempt n plus 1 with the merge-main instruction (shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner), and the new head re-arms this node.

A refusal by a branch rule is not retried on the same head (F10): strict protection with main moved is behind and goes to update-branch on fresh state; any other refusal is a system-lane fault shown by N-41 and one card.
A merge.held is not a failure and is not retried by this node: every held pull request is re-examined on every tick.
retries.report: Every then clause is a record; nothing is silent and nothing loops (merge.sh choice 6: a gh outage posts one blocked record, not one per pull request).

many-agents.readers: Any number of seats read merge records; a worker brief for a merge-main attempt cites the merge.conflict id.
many-agents.two-traversals: Two traversals for the same head both try the merge.lock lease; one gets it, the other ends. If the lock expires mid-call, the second holder finds the effects row N-09/merge/pr@head/r1 already present and reconciles it (step 8b) instead of sending; the operation key makes the record write a replay.
many-agents.two-pulls: Two pull requests ready at once: the first merges; the second is merge.held awaiting-verify until N-10 verifies or rejects the first, then reads a fresh mergeable_state (behind goes to update-branch and a new head, which is re-gated and re-reviewed; dirty goes to its worker). This is the one-file one-in-flight rule's safety net, not its replacement: N-03 refuses overlapping claims before any seat starts (V07).
many-agents.stale-review: A review.passed posted with a token that is not current is refused by N-01 (412); this node never sees it. A review on an older head is held, never merged.
many-agents.hold-race: N-10 writes merge.hold, or N-44 sets flag:hold on an N-29 ruling, while a traversal is between step 2 and step 8: the step 8 Commit re-reads both as preconditions and refuses; the remaining window is closed by GitHub, which requires coq/gate on the head.
many-agents.fix-under-hold: Two fix pull requests naming one hold cannot both exist: N-03 refuses a second fix ticket naming a hold until the first is verified or dead (../N-10/spec.xml#many-agents). If one still appears, step 3 lets only one merge before N-10 judges it.
many-agents.conflict-reports: Every 409 on a key and every lease refusal is logged with the key; never a silent overwrite.
many-agents.test: Test case two-traversals-one-merge: two Merge calls with a fake forge and one lease write one merge record, one merge call and one lease refusal (checklist c-one-merge).

emits.acts: N-26 verifies main; N-45 cleans up; N-03 moves the ticket to merged
nobody; the new head is gated and reviewed as any pushed head; N-39 shows it
N-11 schedules the worker's merge-main attempt
nobody; N-39 and N-41 show it
N-41 alerts; N-28 one card (system lane)
N-41 alerts; N-28 coalesces with N-10's card by hold id

reads.acts: this node merges only the fix pull request whose ticket entity names the hold id; every other merge is held
this node merges nothing while it stands

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE as in ../N-07/spec.xml#state-paths; path elements in N-45's generator form.
state-paths.path: Rows: merge, branch.update, merge.conflict, merge.held, merge.failed records; this node's effects rows; the merge.lock lease; the merge_seq counter. Merge records are never pruned before their verified record and the retention window.
One line per step with the GitHub response status; rotated daily.
state-paths.never: No worktree, no checkout of main, no branch deletion here (N-45 owns those paths and their cleanup); no file under the repository.

in.record: forge:snapshot entity, forge_pr_files, forge.pr_closed, protection.observed, protection.drift

in.note: read, not consumed: the hold and the awaiting-verify step
read, not consumed; decides the two exceptions

schema.defs: review_passed (the fields of N-19's record this node relies on, with lease as lease_ref), merge (parent_main, base_sha, fix_for_hold_id, bootstrap_step), branch_update, merge_conflict, merge_failed, merge_held, merge_hold_aged; base ../N-07/record.schema.json#/$defs/base.

item.proof: go test ./internal/merge -run TestDecision over a table of records, entities and heads; same inputs, same decision

checklist.item: The merge is a pure function of records and the head.

item.proof: test TestStaleReviewHeld: a review on an older head yields merge.held stale-review and no GitHub call

checklist.item: A head pushed after the review is held.

item.proof: test TestHoldBeforeAndAfter: a hold written between step 2 and step 8 refuses the step 8 Commit
test TestFixMergesUnderHold: with a standing hold H, a pull request whose ticket entity has hold_id H merges and carries fix_for_hold_id H; a sibling and one with a lifted hold's id are held

checklist.item: Only the fix pull request merges under a hold.

item.proof: test TestBootstrapMerge: under flag:hold with bootstrap:state B4, a ticket of step B4 merges with bootstrap_step B4; a ticket of B5 and a product ticket are held owner-hold; not-run

checklist.item: The bootstrap merge path is exactly one step wide.

item.proof: test TestAwaitingVerify (AT-F13): merges fed faster than the main run; each waits merge.held awaiting-verify until N-10's verdict; a red main lets only its fix merge; not-run

checklist.item: At most one unverified merge on main.

item.proof: test TestBehindUpdates (AT-F10): two disjoint PRs at one base, both green; the first merges, the second gets one update-branch, a new head, a new gate and review, then merges; no merge call on the stale head; not-run

checklist.item: Behind is brought up to date, never retried.

item.proof: test TestProtectionUnverified: a protection.drift newer than the observed record, and an observed record older than two check intervals, each hold every merge

checklist.item: Protection is verified before any call.

item.proof: test TestFilesUnknown: no forge_pr_files rows, and files_truncated true, each hold files-unknown; owner-locked paths without a promotion.confirm ruling hold awaiting-owner-confirm

checklist.item: The owner-confirm rule never runs on an empty list.

item.proof: test TestHoldAged with the fake clock: a hold standing past merge.hold_age_alert_seconds writes one merge.hold.aged and a second tick writes none

checklist.item: The hold wait has a bound and reports once.

item.proof: test TestTwoTraversalsOneMerge writes one merge record and sends one merge call
test TestLostReply (AT-F16): a timeout after GitHub merged; step 8b finds it through forge.pr_closed and through GET pulls/N and writes once; no second call

checklist.item: A lost reply is reconciled, not repeated.

item.proof: test TestConflictOncePerHead: three traversals on one dirty head write one 409

the forge-merge token is read only by internal/merge; a grep of every other package for COQ_FORGE_MERGE_TOKEN returns nothing; against a scratch repository the forge-read token's merge call answers 403 (AT-F08); not-run
grep of internal/merge finds no git worktree, branch delete or checkout call
every GitHub call in internal/merge carries a context deadline of 20 s; no time.Sleep
config key merge.enabled false until the go-live ticket; while false the node writes merge.held reason dark and merges nothing

permissions.process: The Go service user unit (coq-svc) with the forge-merge credential (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix: contents and pull requests write on the one repository; no administration, no statuses, no secrets, no workflow).
permissions.reads: gate.verdict, review.passed, forge.pr_closed, protection.observed, protection.drift, merge.hold, verified, rejected, halt records; the forge:snapshot entity and forge_pr_files; flag:hold and bootstrap:state; the ticket entity; the merge.lock lease; this node's effects rows.
permissions.writes: merge, branch.update, merge.conflict, merge.held, merge.failed, merge.hold.aged, store.unreachable records; tickets.transition pr_open to merged; effects rows; the merge log; at most one merge call per head and at most merge.update_branch_per_hour update-branch calls per pull request.
permissions.never: No branch deletion, no worktree, no local git, no herdr call, no pane, no protection change, no status post, no edit of any record.
permissions.seat: No seat holds forge-merge; the seat layer (N-13) denies gh pr merge and the merge API; N-01 refuses kind merge from any principal but the service.

gauge.name: merge_ready_held
gauge.from: pull requests with green plus review and a merge.held newest, by reason

lamp.name: merge
lamp.green: no merge.held older than 2 x tick other than awaiting-verify inside its bound, and no merge.failed open
lamp.amber: a merge.hold stands (N-10) or a merge awaits verify
lamp.red: merge.failed open, protection-unverified, or store unreachable

alert.to: N-41 and one card by N-28
N-41 with the hold's sha and age; the card is N-10's
N-41; the card is N-04's protection.drift
N-41; N-28 coalesces with N-10's card by hold id

runbook.bring-up: N-08 live, N-19 posting review.passed, N-25's coq-gate app and the owner's protection in place with a protection.observed from N-04; forge-merge in STATE/secrets/forge-merge; set merge.enabled true; proof: a merge record whose merge_sha is the head of main on GitHub and whose parent_main equals the previous main.
runbook.read-status: Scheduler.Status lists pull requests ready, held with reason, conflicting and merged in the last hour; the Machine screen shows one pull request's path.
runbook.recover-github-down: Nothing by hand: unknown effects rows are reconciled by step 8b when N-04 polls succeed; a merged-but-unrecorded pull request is completed from forge.pr_closed.
runbook.recover-stuck-lock: A merge.lock lease expires after merge.lock_seconds 300 on its own; never delete a lease by hand.
runbook.recover-red-main: Nothing by hand: N-10 cuts the fix ticket through a spec-author run and this node merges its pull request under the hold (step 2 exception); a green main lifts the hold. After three failed fixes the owner's one card carries the recommendation.
runbook.recover-protection: A protection-unverified hold clears by itself when N-04 writes a protection.observed; repairing protection is the owner's forge-admin task (N-04 runbook protection.drift card).
runbook.break-glass: A merge the owner wants despite a hold, or a hold the owner wants lifted, is a control.action through N-42 (one time, recorded); a hand gh pr merge leaves no merge record, and N-10 fails closed on a sha the store does not know (N-10 step 6); N-51 counts it.
runbook.registry: Generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json from the state-paths element (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths); branch and worktree cleanup entries are N-45's own.

source.use: outcomes, exit codes, choices 1 to 6, the hold choices 1 to 4, post_merge_clean: lifted nearly unchanged (L01 section 8 item 3)
heads_match and same-head predicates; events/ excluded from the tree compare
option B: machine verdict merges, owner holds via cards
GitHub refuses a merge without a green gate
V03 merge and verify as pure functions with a hold file; V07 one file one in-flight ticket
item 3 merge.sh as the template; item 4 gate.sh predicates; item 6 claims
D11 merge a PR with both gate records: 43 of 92 by hand; D20 merger seat
do not build a global-lock merge queue first; conflict repair by a fresh seat
